title: Find Repeating Characters: Early Win, Long Regression
description: A student reaches public success early, then repeatedly regresses and finishes with a partial private score.
why_interesting: Strong example of regression: apparent progress does not hold under hidden tests or later edits.

source.question_title: Find Characters Appearing More Than Once

timeline.text: Goal: return characters that repeat. The session opens with runtime issues, common in first drafts.
Public tests all pass surprisingly early. It may feel “done” at this point.
Immediate private failure (33). Hidden cases likely include duplicates/order behavior not captured in public checks.
Now public quality drops too. This suggests the fix attempts are destabilizing previously working parts.
Private remains at zero in the middle phase. They may be changing code structure without re-validating invariants.
Still wrong-answer heavy deep into the session. Effort is high, but feedback loops are weak.
Late-stage private checks still fail. A key lesson: repeated execution is not the same as targeted debugging.
Final submission ends at 33. Useful example for teaching regression control and checkpoint-based debugging.
